Consider the ellipse $E$ and vector field $F$ shown above. Let $C$ be any path where $E$ is traversed once in the **clockwise** direction. Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We now recall the following:

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.
$$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.
$$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statements $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0
$$ and $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0
$$ are false. Since the force $F$ acts perpendicular to the motion of the particle as it moves around $C,$ it neither helps nor hinders its motion. 

![](images/04/045f6867a50dff0c162376015cc4651de796d0a637643b4b5ba402ef55dde4fa.png)

So, $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

- Statement $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0
$$ is true. If we reverse the orientation of $C,$ then the situation with regards to the work done by $F$ remains unchanged.

![](images/69/698f68b9539e6ef5c4b07dbe6cf3859449e2687db19406f6c2b0072fa5eb697e.png)

So, $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is $$
\displaystyle {∮}_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0
$$ only.

question.:question/problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=2x\,i+2y\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=9$ oriented counterclockwise.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we write the equation of our curve as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1.
$$

The closed curve $C$ is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $3$ and $1,$ respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2x\,i+2y\,j \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }-16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8\left(\frac{-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}\right)\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-4(-1+1) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
